title: Context-loss triage: lossy compression scratchpad
content:
Quick purpose: scribble practical heuristics and tiny experiments for 'lossy' context compression that we can ship as a lightweight preprocessor for multi-turn apps. Not a full paper — half thinking-out-loud, half runbook.

Topline ideas (brain-dump):
- Goal: reduce token budget for long multi-turn conversations while preserving surface-level coherence and hallucination-resistance for task-oriented flows (agent calls, tickets, shopping, docs).
- Why lossy: full retention + exact KV caching is heavy and brittle for app UX; small, controlled forgetting + summarization can drastically cut cost with little UX impact.

Heuristics to try (ordered by simplicity):
1) Landmark-turn retention: always keep the last N turns + any turns with explicit 'action' markers ("call API", "decision:"). N tuned by model size / latency SLO.
2) Slot-summary injection: extract slot-value pairs from recent turns (task-specific) and replace raw text with compact KV lines. E.g., "customer: Jane; intent: refund; order: #4321".
3) Compressed windowing via sentence-level importance: compute TF-IDF-ish score across convo -> crop low-score sentences. Fast and deterministic.
4) Lowbit semantic hashing: project turn embeddings to 32-bit hash; when similarity > threshold, deduplicate earlier turn.
5) Progressive summarization: every K turns, insert a 1–3 sentence summary and drop detailed turns older than that checkpoint. Keep checkpoints until conversational pivot.
6) Event anchors: if external events (calendar invites, tool outputs) referenced, keep anchors and brief context, drop surrounding chit-chat.

Initial experiments (micro):
- Dataset: 200 multi-turn helpdesk threads (internal anonymized). Vary: N in landmark retention (2,4,6), slot coverage heuristics on top-10 slots.
- Metrics: task success (proxy via single-turn eval), hallucination rate (model asserts facts not in retained context), latency, token count reduction. Also human perceived coherence (small blind eval, 5 judges).
- Baselines: full last-2048 tokens, naive truncate tail, simple summarization (gpt-lite compress).

Implementation notes / cheap prototypes:
- Start as preprocessing module in Rust/Python, run before request goes to serving runtime. Keep deterministic pipeline for auditability.
- Use our embeddings endpoint for sentence importance (batch) but cache results hashed by conversation id + turn hash.
- Keep a tiny-state metadata: last_checkpoint_ts, [anchor_ids], slot_map(serialized). That helps rehydration.

Open research-y concerns (for later):
- Quantized embedding drift: when using int8 embeddings for fast hashing, similarity noise can hurt dedup decisions; need calibration.
- Summaries as new context: summaries can introduce abstraction errors — consider mismatch detection by cross-checking summary-derived facts with original turns via entailment model.
- Privacy: explicit redaction/PII handling when compressing. Summaries must not resurrect PII from dropped turns. Add opt-out per-customer.

Short pseudocode (sketch):
- ingest(turn): append to buffer; if turn.has_action_markers -> mark anchor; if len(buffer) > max_window -> run compress_if_needed();
- compress_if_needed(): extract slots -> rewrite buffer with slots + anchors + last_N_turns + checkpoint_summaries; return tokenized size estimate;

Checklist for first sprint (2 weeks):
- [ ] implement landmark-turn retention pipeline (N configurable) -> measure token reduction on corpus
- [ ] simple slot extractor using regex + small NER fallback -> test on helpdesk data
- [ ] run human coherence quick eval (50 threads) comparing baseline vs. landmark+slots
- [ ] add telemetry fields: pre_tokens, post_tokens, dropped_turn_ids, compression_strategy
- [ ] draft playbook page on Confluence (link above) describing safety checks and rollback knobs

Quick notes to self about edge cases:
- Long quoted blocks (logs) should be summarized with header like "(log excerpt, 120 tokens)" rather than included.
- If user explicitly asks "remember X for later", treat as sticky slot. Add explicit confirmation channel in UI.
- System messages that seed behavior should always be preserved even if older (we've tripped on this before).

Relevant papers + notes (rough):
- paper: "Chunking and Summarizing Long Dialogues" — idea: periodic abstractive summaries help downstream. Implementation caution: abstractive summaries introduce false precision.
- paper: "KV Compression for Long-Context LMs" — technical approaches for compressing KV caches; worth linking to eng PR.
- blog: "Practical Context Pruning for Chatbots" (quick heuristics list; good starting point for product-friendly rules).

Questions to raise in sync with Mira / Noah:
- What token-reduction target feels 'safe' for core customers? 3x? 5x? need product input.
- Which customers want sticky memory vs ephemeral? default config should favor ephemeral unless opt-in.

Notes from quick smoke run (toy):
- landmark N=4 + slots reduced median tokens by ~2.6x on helpdesk set. Some drop in exact slot recall (4%); hallucination unchanged in 50-thread sample. Needs bigger run.
- Worst failures: summaries overwritten actionable details (e.g., refund amount). Add slot-check and explicit numerical slot preservation.

Ideas for productization (longer horizon):
- Expose compression level as per-route config in Redwood Console (slider: lenient|balanced|conservative).
- Autotune per-route with cost+latency SLO signals; fallback to larger retention if user reports regression.
- Offer a "compaction report" for compliance: show dropped_turns, summary text, and rationale.

Todo (next steps):
- Pair with Noah next Monday to implement N-curve sweep + telemetry.
- Draft short README for SEs explaining safe knobs.
- Put up a quick demo in /playgrounds/kakapo-ctx-compress showing live token savings.

Random scratch ideas (worth remembering):
- 'temporal bucketing' — keep denser detail for recent 10 turns, sparser for 11-50 (coastline-like retention).
- 'rehearsal buffer' — keep one 'reminder' synthetic turn every K turns that lists unresolved items.

End-of-file notes: this doc is personal scratchpad; will convert into a canonical playbook if results look promising.

-- lucy
